title: Halibut with White Bean and Dill Cream
description: Mashed white beans give this dill cream body without heavy cream.
equipment: Ninja Crispi, 4-qt glass container and adapter

steps.title: Simmer the sauce
steps.text: Whisk {beans}, {broth}, {milk} into the HexClad. Simmer gently for 5 minutes and blend smooth with an immersion blender.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Whisk {starch} with {cold}, then stir into the simmering sauce for 1 minute until it coats a spoon.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Remove from the heat and whisk in {dill} until evenly incorporated.

steps.title: Prepare the dish
steps.text: Start with the room-temperature 4-qt glass container, no crisper plate. Let sauce cool to lukewarm before adding to the glass. Spread the sauce over the base.

steps.title: Portion the fish
steps.text: Arrange {halibut} in two even pieces about ¾ inch thick.

steps.title: Cook in sauce
steps.text: Nestle the pieces in the sauce in a single layer. Fit the 4-qt adapter and PowerPod and select Bake. Cook for 10–15 minutes, checking the thickest piece early. Finish at 145°F in the center.

steps.title: Serve generously
steps.text: Spoon hot sauce over each serving.

notes: Make ahead: prepare the sauce a day ahead and refrigerate separately. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze cooked portions with sauce, cooled within 2 hours, for up to 2 months. Flaky fish is best freshly cooked; thaw slowly and keep covered. Fridge reheat: cover and warm gently with a spoonful of water to 165°F. Freezer reheat: thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat covered to 165°F. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For gentler Option B, omit added citrus, vinegar or chile where used. Pass additional heat at the table. Dairy swap: use unsweetened oat milk and equivalent plain dairy-free cheese if needed. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 179 kcal, 27.4 g protein, 12.1 g total carbohydrate, 1.8 g fat, 2.0 g fiber, 105 mg sodium.
